top.line: A reply to Florent Daudens: sell capabilities, not content.
top.para: The storm site and PrompTugal.news by place show what the products can be.

in-short.line: His question, his answer, the storm site, local sites, our answers, and a second reply.

question.line: Publishers have the protocols; Florent asks where the products are.
question.para: Sell capabilities; connect subscriptions to personal agents.

storm.line: 2,618 pages in three days, every fact sourced and timed, possible only because of the method built before it.
storm.para: Conductors, roles, hand-overs, files as memory, keys and lanes, release gates and observability: the speed was the dividend of that structure.

place.line: A site per town, each a lens on one graph: a product for a town and its agents.
place.para: 73 signed articles in ten days, now going local.

answers.line: Agent-readable pages, keys people own, licences and policies, a meter, signatures.
answers.para: Working pieces, not a finished product.

next.line: Subscriptions as keys, lenses sold as capabilities, and decision graphs.
next.para: The paywall as a permission, not a login page.

limits.line: A strategy for local sites; our own working pieces; his post summarised.

sources.line: Florent Daudens' post and LinkedIn, and our earlier articles.
sources.para: With a link to our first reply.
